method_steps: Build the ledger and infer the profile with confidence grades (phase 1)
Code postings on 35 requirement codes, second-code a sample, score liveness (phase 3)
Peers (phase 4) — fictional peer set for the two run-now niches (19 people); a real run collects them from public announcements, team pages and speaker bios
Then vs now on closed postings (phase 5)
Fit, qualification and ranking with 1,000 weight draws (phase 6)
Four niche resumes from one ledger (phase 8)
Gates, advocate test and CEO review loops (phase 9)
limits: Fictional candidate; postings are the real reference corpus, so volume thresholds were relaxed to 8 postings / 5 employers.
All niches have fewer than 30 coded postings: statistical tests are off and changes are directional.
Raw posting text was not retained in the reference run; codes cannot be re-audited from text.
Access paths are inferred from shared ecosystems in the postings, not from a real network.
The peers in act 3 are fictional, generated from the niches' own requirement rates; the postings are real.
Recruiter and hiring-manager reviewers not run in the example; two CEO loops were.

sources.title: Reference corpus: 42 coded 2026 postings and 17 closed 2020–25 postings

Interview Guys review of negotiation studies

acts.question: What can the market do with a record like Jordan's?
acts.answer: We read 42 live job postings across four markets and placed Jordan's record among them, star by star.
acts.handover: It starts with what Jordan brings.

acts.question: What does Jordan bring, on the evidence?
acts.answer: A builder of partner programs who has worked on three sides of the partner market and builds working AI tools without being an engineer.
learned: Six strengths are stated outright on the resume, each traced to a line of it.
Thirteen years in partnerships, the most recent role leading a team of four partner managers.
The current resume undersells this: no role says what the employer sells or how big it is.
acts.handover: That is the supply. Now, who is asking for it?

acts.question: Who is asking for it, and what do they want?
acts.answer: Four markets share one core: ten requirements appear in at least half the postings of every niche, and Jordan proves seven of them.
learned: Every niche asks for owned partner revenue and technology partners; Jordan proves both.
Working for an AI product company and senior-executive relationships are asked everywhere and do not show on the resume.
One listing in ten in the top niche shows signs of not being a real opening, below the 18–22% platform benchmark.
acts.handover: That is the demand. Who else is answering it?

acts.question: Who else supplies this, and what is rare about Jordan?
acts.answer: Jordan is in range of the people already doing these jobs: they have a median of 12 years, Jordan has 13. The clearest edge over them is owned partner revenue: 88% of postings ask for it, 58% of these peers show it.
learned: Most came from partner roles at martech platforms or AI providers; Jordan's path through an agency, a platform and a data vendor is less common.
The top two niches hire at Head and VP level, one band above Jordan's current title.
Referrals convert about eleven times better than cold applications: this field is won on access, not volume.
acts.handover: Supply, demand, competition. Here is what they add up to.

acts.question: Where should Jordan aim, and why?
acts.answer: Two niches now, two next: the Head roles in New York lead, the director roles and Paris follow.
learned: The martech and data Head niche ranks first on fit, pay and demand together.
The top three keep their order in 58% of 1,000 random re-weightings: the top two are close, and both are worth running.
acts.handover: The decision is made. Here is how to run it.

acts.question: What exactly does Jordan do, send and say?
acts.answer: Fill the blanks, send the two Head versions to the gold-star postings first, and log every approach so the tracker can say what to change.

acts.question: How was this measured, and what are its limits?
acts.answer: 42 live and 17 archive postings coded on one codebook by two independent coders, agreement κ 0.79; every resume line traced to the original.
